label: EXPLAINED (corrected)
role: DeepSeekV3-style MoE routing for <=4 tokens (top-8 of 256 experts, permutation/histogram outputs); 75 calls per decode step; identical kernel and launch (1x256) in vLLM.
pcvs: tokens 1..4, local experts 128/256, tile tokens 8/16, TK = tokens*8
finding: One CTA of 256 lanes. Exact: global_read_bytes = 260*TK, unique = 128*TK + 1024, fp32_flops = 649*TK, block barriers = 9 per launch (2304 lane arrivals), collective arrivals 84*TK + 608. The first latency model reported a fixed chain of 17 dependent global loads (10344..10596 units); with the critical-lane chain and -lineinfo source lines this turned out to be a model artifact: the loads are guarded by short forward branches (RoutingKernel.cuh:127 score loads behind idx<numExperts, RoutingCustomPolicy.cuh:234 bias loads in a dtype switch) that ptxas predicates. With if-conversion modeled the path is 2763 units (one exposed load plus barriers): the kernel is short on its own, consistent with vLLM's 4.5 us, so our 22 us/call in graph (1.57 ms/step) is queuing - the shared-expert GEMMs are enqueued first on the side stream and the 1-CTA routing kernel waits for an SM.
fix: Scheduling (gen-glm53-decode-step): GLM53_DECODE_ROUTED_FIRST enqueues the routed path before the shared expert; GLM53_DECODE_ROUTED_PRIORITY gives the main decode streams the greatest priority, the shared-expert stream the least, and instantiates graphs with cudaGraphInstantiateFlagUseNodePriority (1654 high / 300 low priority kernel nodes captured).
timing: b114 B300 harness: routing 23.0 -> 17.0 us/call (routed first) / 16.6 us (priority); step -0.22..-0.24 ms (routed first) and -0.26..-0.32 ms (priority) uniform, -0.24..-0.32 ms hot; the deprioritized shared down GEMM slows 5.3 -> 24.9 us off the critical path. CUPTI interval analysis: routing launches ~5 us before its producer moe_front_prenorm ends (PDL); measured from the producer end it takes 14.4 us (control) -> 8.8 us (either fix), still ~4.3 us over vLLM while sharing SMs with already-running GEMM CTAs.
reproduce: see gpu/examples/moe_routing (results/run1); latency: python3 gpu/tools/latency_report.py results/run1
credit: DrPerf explained why the kernel has a fixed ~latency floor; the contention with the side stream comes from the CUPTI timeline. Tool gaps found: drperf_gpu.h dim3 clashed with CUDA headers in nvcc-compiled drivers (fixed); latency metrics are per-launch diagnostics without per-site attribution of exposed loads.
